title.narrative: Core Support to Transparency International Georgia 2018-2021

description.narrative: The overall objective of the intervention is defined as "to support building and empowering state institutions, develop good governance and the rule of law, ensure the transparency and direct accountability of the state institutions, support fair and democratic elections (for this aim including election observations) and protect universally recognized human rights". For achieving overall objectives the intervention plans to achieve few specific objectives: Objective 1: Contribute to reduced opportunities for corruption (including high-level corruption) in the executive branch Objective 2: Contribute to greater transparency and accountability in local government Objective 3: Promote transparency, accountability, and integrity in Parliament and effectiveness of Parliament as an oversight institution Objective 4: Promote more pluralistic political system through greater transparency and accountability in political parties and more competitive and fair elections Objective 5: Promote independence, transparency, accountability, and integrity in the justice system Objective 6: Promoting independence, professionalism and investigative activities of journalists to empower media as an anti-corruption watchdog Objective 7: Counter anti-Western propaganda and promote unbiased information about Georgia’s European and Euro-Atlantic integration Outcome targets for those specific objectives are given in the result matrix. They are assessed as achievable, given that external risks associated with slow down of Georgia's overall reform process not will be materialised and the country will continue its reforms and its way on developing democratic, accountable and transparent governance.

Transparency International (TI) Georgia applied to the Embassy for funding in form of core support for the years 2018 - 2021 with a volume of 15 000 000 SEK.
TI Geogia works in the area of anti-corruption and good governance with the aim to increase transparency and accountability in national and local government in Georgia. TI works through advocacy, monitoring and capacity building in close cooperation with both state actors and civil society.
TI Georgia believes that its activities as a watch dog and think tank in areas of anti-corruption policy, judicial reform, parliamentary democracy, local government, elections, political and campaign finance, media, economic policy will lead to reducing opportunities for corruption through transparency, accountability and integrity in key institutions in Georgia that is ultimate goal of the intervention.
The overall objective of the intervention is defined as "to support building and empowering state institutions, develop good governance and the rule of law, ensure the transparency and direct accountability of the state institutions, support fair and democratic elections (for this aim including election observations) and protect universally recognized human rights". The intervention objective is assessed as relevant to the Swedish strategy and its support to Georgia.
This will be phase two of the core support provided to TI Georgia, the phase one of the support lasted 2015-2017 and it was assessed as successful and having contributed to Georgia´s democratic development.

Transparency International (TI) har ansökt om kärnstöd för perioden 2018-2021 med en total budget på 15 MSEK.
Genom att arbeta med antikorruption och god samhällsstyrning strävar TI efter att öka transparens och ansvarsutkrävande inom regeringen på både nationell och lokal nivå. TI arbetar med påverkansarbete, uppföljning och kapacitetsuppbyggnad i nära samarbete med såväl statliga aktörer som med civilsamhälleorganisationer.
TI anser att de aktiviteter som de genomför som tankesmedja och Watch-dog, genom att arbeta med transparens, ansvarsutkrävande och integritet inom nyckelinstitutionerna i Georgien, kommer att minska korruption inom viktiga områden som rättsväsendet, parlamentarisk demokrati, lokala myndigheter, valprocesser, politisk finansiering, media och ekonomisk politik.
Insatsens huvudsyfte är att ”bidra till uppbyggande och förstärkande av statliga institutioner, utveckla god samhällsstyrning och rättssäkerhet, upprätthålla transparens och ansvarsutkrävande inom statliga institutioner, stödja rättvisa och demokratiska valprocesser (inklusive valobservation) och "försvara internationellt erkända mänskliga rättigheter ”. Insatsens mål anses vara relevant för genomförande av Resultatstrategin.
Detta kommer att vara fas två av kärnstödet till TI Georgia. Fas 1 pågick under 2015-2017 och bedömdes vara både framgångsrik och anses ha bidragit till Georgiens demokratiska utveckling.

Objective 1: Contribute to reduced opportunities for corruption (including high-level corruption) in the executive branch
- TI Georgia was the first to raise alarm about the signs of increasing high-level corruption and state capture some years ago, a position which is now widely shared on both local and international levels largely due to TI Georgia research, investigation and advocacy efforts. Responding to the challenge TI Georgia developed a legislative proposal to set up an independent anti-corruption agency.
- TI Georgia identified and studied more specific areas that are vulnerable to corruption, producing evidence-based reports and developing solutions. The areas covered in this way included: whistleblower protection, conflict of interest, asset declaration system, revolving door, beneficial ownership transparency.
- In 2019, TI Georgia analyzed the Georgian Governments compliance with its anti-corruption commitments under the Association Agreement and the Association Agenda. The report found that the Government largely failed to implement the reforms necessary to achieve the goals and objectives set out in the Agreement and the Agenda.
Objective 2: Contribute to greater transparency and accountability in local government
- TI Georgia further expanded its regional presence in order to contribute to an improved standard of transparency and accountability in local governments. It runs by the end of the project 5 regional offices throughout Georgia in Batumi, Kutaisi, Zugdidi, Telavi and Akhaltsikhe.
- TI Georgia systemically monitored the work and the expenditure of the local government bodies and highlighted alleged schemes of corruption and the possible cases of misuse of the state funds where recent and former government officials and/or their families were involved.
- TI Georgia tried to improve the level of accountability of local city councils and executive bodies not only with monitoring but also with cooperation and capacity-building tools. Between 2018 and 2021 up to 12 training sessions were designed and implemented with up to 150 participants, representing local municipalities.
Objective 3: Promote transparency, accountability, and integrity in Parliament and effectiveness of Parliament as an oversight institution
- TI Georgia annually observed the performance of the Georgian Parliament and identified several shortcomings related to its work, including the weak role of the opposition in decision making, issues of accountability and responsibility of both MPs and members of the government. The monitoring led to presenting our recommendations to the Parliament of Georgia, contributing to more transparency and accountability of the institution.
- Between 2018 ad 2021 TI Georgia released analyses/publications of 43 problematic bills and submitted recommendations to the Parliament for taking them into consideration during discussions. Those publications were followed by 23 roundtable discussions on the important developments.
- TI Georgia served as a member of the consultative group under the Gender Equality Council at the Parliament of Georgia and annually monitored councils work, published in-depth reports and provided specific recommendations.
- Between 2018 and 2021, TI Georgia published 3 special reports on parliamentary oversight. Based on its monitoring and best international practice research, TI Georgia presented recommendations to the Parliament of Georgia and identified a number of shortcomings.
Objective 4: Promote more pluralistic political system through greater transparency and accountability in political parties and more competitive and fair elections
- TI Georgia collected evidence on the misuse of administrative resources and financial inequality among political parties. TI Georgia has been trying to regularly expose these problems by providing comprehensive reports on election legislation reforms as well as electoral processes.
- TI Georgia organized large-scale observing missions for 2018 Presidential, 2020 Parliamentary, and 2021 Municipal elections. Between 2018 and 2020, we managed to deploy up to 400 observers throughout the country for each general election held in Georgia, thus contributing to the transparent and fair electoral process during the election day.
Objective 5: Promote independence, transparency, accountability, and integrity in the justice system
- TI Georgia exposed through numerous reports, studies and statements (the report on the promotions in Georgian judiciary, report on development in judiciary and report on the management of the specialization and case allocation) clan based rule at the judiciary. Eventually, TI Georgia achieved the result when the general public, various stakeholders and international actors became aware of the main challenges, particularly the unlimited powers of the group of influential judges and its consequences.
Objective 6: Promoting independence, professionalism and investigative activities of journalists to empower media as an anti-corruption watchdog
- TI Georgia has exposed the whole scale of the problems facing the media, namely the concerns regarding physical safety, the government's failure to investigate the cases of violence against media representatives, illegal surveillance as well as various methods of pressure on critical and independent media. As a result of TI Georgia monitoring and assessment, it was found out that during the past two years alone, up to 100 cases of violence against media took place and the government has failed to take preventive measures and ensure the proper investigation to hold the perpetrators accountable.
- TI Georgia conducted a series of capacity-building sessions aimed at increasing investigative skills and knowledge for journalists and activists. The training beneficiaries were Tbilisi and regional-based media professionals, as well as aspiring journalists and civic activists. During the reporting period TI Georgia contributed to the enhanced capacity of up to 400 media professionals.
Objective 7: Counter anti-Western propaganda and promote unbiased information about Georgias European and Euro-Atlantic integration
- TI Georgia facilitated the process of forming the Coalition for Euro-Atlantic Georgia, composed of 25 civil society organizations with various scopes of work and target groups. All of the members of the coalition were united around the idea of promoting Georgias Euro-Atlantic integration and were committed to coordinating efforts and join forces to counter disinformation. Between 2018 and 2021 TI Georgia served as the chair of the board of the coalition for 2 times and directed coalition efforts towards countering disinformation and promoting pro-Western messages.
